typed_id.description: Value of an explicit, domain-typed identifier. The property name carries the domain; a bare product_id or user_id is forbidden at a cross-skill boundary.

schema.description: One operation row as declared by the central registry at 44-convert-and-flow-operator/tools/engine/cli_anything/gohighlevel/public/operations.py. Additive v1: every field the operation contract requires (Document 1 section 5.1) is declared per row, never inferred from the HTTP verb or from a module-wide default. `x-semantic-constraints` records checks a JSON Schema cannot express and that the contract validator enforces.

availability_restriction.description: Named blocker/restriction code. Documentation never activates a tenant.

doc_evidence.description: Provenance of doc_url and doc_retrieved_at. revision3_spec means the contract came from the revision-3 specification without reopening the page; it must never be reported as a fresh fetch.

effect.description: Read/write effect of the operation itself, independent of method. POST /workflows/search is a read; definition validation persists nothing but consumes write quota.

identity_binding.description: The frozen tenant_binding literal, e.g. path.locationId, query.locationId, body.locationId, implicit-pit, token-id, connection scope, n/a, unknown.

identity_placement.description: Where the tenant/location identity rides. Never inferred from the verb.

method.description: POST/DELETE is a documented dual-verb row (like/unlike); UNKNOWN is an unresolved operation whose path is a named capability gap.

readback_operation.description: Operation id that proves a write. null means no frozen readback plan; the caller must supply one.

request_media_type.description: The real request media type. A typed JSON request and a typed multipart request can never be confused.

scopes.description: Candidate scopes from evidence. An empty array means the scope is unresolved, never that no scope is needed.

unresolved_fields.description: Declared fields whose evidence did not settle them. Named explicitly, never guessed.

version.description: Per-operation Version header literal. null means the route sends no Version header (official MCP rows) or has no public contract.

schema.title: GHL Hybrid Operation Contract
x-semantic-constraints: identity_placement must agree with identity_binding's leading segment (path./query./body./implicit-pit/token-id/connection scope/n/a/unknown).
token_class must agree with token_class_derived(auth_kinds).
effect=write requires approval_class != none for a destructive route and requires the registry write flag.
scopes_resolved=false is required whenever scopes is empty.
implementation must agree with route_class through TRANSPORT_BY_ROUTE.

then.description: A write capability additionally requires a passed write canary; the JSON Schema cannot branch on whether the operation is a write, so the validator enforces that rule.

contract_revision.description: The operation-contract hash this capability was evaluated against.

credential_ref.description: Alias only, e.g. location-pit:OWNER_MANAGED_ALIAS. Never a secret value.

principal.description: Authenticated principal identity (token-derived), never a secret.

schema.description: Additive v2 capability record (Document 1 section 5.2). Separate facts replace one misleading `enabled` boolean: documentation, adapter existence, offline tests, account availability, authorization/scope evidence, a bounded read probe and a bounded write canary are independent dimensions. A read on one location never activates another location, and documentation never enables a tenant. v1 records are translated by `legacy_conversion` without widening any grant; the v1 `capabilities` map is not rewritten in place.

capabilities.description: operation_id -> capability facts for this one location.

legacy_conversion.description: Provenance of a v1 -> v2 translation. A v1 record is read, never rewritten; the translation is explicit and auditable.

schema.title: GHL Hybrid Capability Record v2
x-semantic-constraints: A capability whose operation effect is write and enabled=true must carry write_canary.state=passed with a receipt_id.
A capability with scope_state in {missing,revoked} must have enabled=false.
checked_at/expires_at are per location/credential/contract; a credential rotation or docs-hash change invalidates only the rows bound to it, never the whole record.
v1 translation maps enabled+read_verified to read_probe.state=passed and leaves write_canary.state=not_run: it never widens a grant.

legacy_conversion.description: Explicit, versioned conversion from a strict old launch binding instead of rewriting it in place.

sub_results.description: Typed per-family results carried inside the one shared envelope.

schema.description: One immutable logical-operation event (Document 1 section 5.5). The stable key is (company_id, location_id, run_id, operation_key); attempts have unique ids underneath it and event_sequence is a persisted increasing integer within the logical operation. Outcomes include unknown_outcome and not_requested and are never mapped onto the Command Center TaskStatus enum. Meeting/AI/KB/widget/Projects sub-results live inside this same envelope; there is no per-feature fork.

content_hash.description: Approved content is hashed separately from redacted diagnostics so redaction cannot invalidate matching.

object_refs.description: Domain-typed object references. Keys must be named typed identifiers, never a bare id/product_id/user_id.

schema.title: GHL Hybrid Operation Receipt v1
x-semantic-constraints: A re-delivered event keeps its original receipt_id and bytes; a later processing/verification update emits a new event and a new event_sequence.
Sequences are allocated by one writer per logical operation; a reducer retains attempt history and applies legal transitions instead of trusting arrival order.
outcome=verified requires readback.state=matched and at least one object ref or evidence ref.
outcome=unknown_outcome forbids a later duplicate write on another rail until reconciliation names the actual object.
Sub-results are optional and independent; a missing sub-result means not requested, never passed.

schema.description: Internal course plan (Document 1 section 8.2). It expresses content and relationships without pretending to be a vendor DTO; Section 8.3 maps it to the public wire contract. Logical keys are the identity inside the plan: duplicate display titles are allowed when logical keys differ. The vendor `status` property is never invented; draft-only release is expressed through module/lesson visibility, offer/access and release actions.

group_ref.description: Relative path to an approved group plan; a standalone course does not require a group.

schema.title: GHL Course Build Plan v1
x-semantic-constraints: module_key is unique across the plan; lesson_key is unique within its module (the same lesson key may appear under different modules).
parent_module_key, when not null, must name a module_key in the same plan; the parent chain must be acyclic and must not point at itself.
description_ref must name a relative path that exists in the approved content set; a missing content reference rejects the plan.
asset_refs must name relative paths in the approved asset set; no cross-location object id may appear.
visibility must be one of the documented category/lesson vocabularies; the two vocabularies are not interchangeable.
Duplicate display titles are allowed when logical keys differ; a matching title is a reconciliation candidate, never permission to edit or delete an existing object.

schema.description: Shared course-media handoff package (Document 1 section 10.3). KIE creates the file; this manifest says which approved file belongs to which lesson, whether generation actually finished, where a durable copy lives, and whether GHL attached it. A queued generation is not completed; a provider URL is not proof that bytes are downloadable, correctly typed and persisted. Required fields vary by asset type: an image never carries an invented audio duration.

proof.description: Separate proofs. A permanent URL proves only asset_persisted.

schema.title: GHL Course Asset Manifest v1
x-semantic-constraints: sha256 is computed from the actual file bytes, never derived from a provider task id.
A completed generation requires a nonzero byte_size, a sha256 and a durable local or approved-storage reference.
ghl_binding.state=association_verified requires both content_id and lesson_id and a readback receipt reference.
Duplicate callbacks or retries update one asset record; they never upload again or create another lesson.

schema.description: Validated course-to-Community-group Learning relationship plan (Document 1 section 9.4). The input is a relationship plan, not a page URL. Attaching and detaching are relationships: detaching never deletes the course, and a group association, a course offer, a commerce product and an enrollment remain separate objects.
schema.title: GHL Learning Association v1
x-semantic-constraints: The group and the course must resolve in the same location; a cross-location reference rejects the plan.
An existing association with the same course and the same access policy produces an idempotent verified result without adding a second one.
operation=detach removes only the relationship and never calls course delete.
Ambiguous name-only matches must be resolved before any UI action; a matching title alone is not object identity.

schema.description: Aggregate course-delivery receipt (Document 1 sections 8.4, 8.5, 17, 18). A filled course title with no content is not delivery. The receipt separates plan-to-object identity, content/media binding, assessments, offer/enrollment, group association, learner access and observed playback. Live verification is reported separately from offline implementation readiness; the reducer that may set business_delivery_verified is the only writer of that state.

live_verification.description: Live learner proof and offline implementation readiness are separate facts.

schema.title: GHL Course Delivery Receipt v1
x-semantic-constraints: business_delivery_verified=true requires outcome=verified, live_verification=passed, and every required component in {verified, not_requested-with-reason}.
A required component in {planned, submitted, processing, failed, blocked, unknown} forbids business_delivery_verified.
A component marked not_requested carries a scope reason; a missing required implementation is never classified not_requested.
plan_object_identity verified requires every approved logical key mapped to a real id (no title-only identity).
